name: Tactile Paper-Motion Brand Explainer — 32-Beat System

provenance.source_kind: Media Lab-owned production template derived from the Automated AI Solutions 112-second paper-motion explainer
provenance.adaptation_note: Generalizes the proven 32-beat company, four-offer, ecosystem, leadership, and closing structure into editable brand slots while retaining the validated tactile motion, pacing, deterministic-text, assembly, and QA contracts.
provenance.usage_note: Private/internal template. The example master remains a review candidate until Steve approves it; template registration does not convert it into an approved final or public asset.

defaults.audio: continuous narration and score assembled in post, with shot-specific tactile Foley
defaults.visual_system: layered tactile paper collage with deterministic printed text and physically plausible stop-motion object movement

brand_promise.default: A clear promise stated in one sentence

palette.default: warm parchment, torn black cardstock, monochrome photography, restrained teal and copper accents

narration_script.description: A time-coded narration script spanning all 32 beats.

score_or_music.description: Optional continuous score or supplied song used during deterministic assembly.

engine_routing.ltx_default: Use LTX for the full first pass, object-led paper movement, wide and medium shots, and rapid same-seed iteration.
engine_routing.h3_upgrade: Use H3 only for selected hero, identity-critical, or difficult high-detail beats that fail the LTX quality gate.
engine_routing.deterministic_post: Use deterministic compositing for exact text, captions, logos, narration, score, Foley, transitions, and the full 112-second assembly.

storyboard_blueprint.title: Brand title reveal
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Reveal {{brand_name}} as deterministic printed artwork.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: A black torn-paper strip rips open across parchment and reveals the company title lockup.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: one dry paper tear, cardstock scrape, quiet room tone

storyboard_blueprint.title: Leadership introduction
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Introduce up to four {{leaders}} with equal visual treatment.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: Four equally monochrome portrait clippings land one by one at four different depths.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: four distinct soft paper slaps, pin clicks

storyboard_blueprint.title: Operating roles
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Pair the leaders with teaching, operations, building, and education role objects.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: A teaching note, operations ledger, technical diagram, and classroom card slide beside the four leaders.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: card slides, pencil ticks, one binder clip click

storyboard_blueprint.title: Brand-to-offer transition
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Transform the company seal into the first offer or capability symbol.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: A circular company seal turns a quarter rotation and its copper center becomes the Source4AI local-AI sphere.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: paper wheel rub, low felt thump

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer A setup
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Unfold the {{offer_a}} workflow and its central promise.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: The blank workflow card unfolds; stitched threads pull toward the glowing local-AI sphere.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: cardstock hinge creak, paper fiber rasp, thread skitter

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer A mechanism
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Show how {{offer_a}} moves from input through local or private execution to human review.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: A graphite path travels from a paper server to a laptop and stops at a human checkpoint token.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: pencil trace, tiny relay ticks, cloth drag

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer A trust proof
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Show the approval, safety, or accountability checkpoint.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: An approval card slides into frame and a wax-paper seal presses once, then settles.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: card slide, single felt-and-paper stamp thump

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer A range
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Show local, hybrid, and cloud options without breaking the supervised workflow.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: Layered local, hybrid, and cloud paper zones separate while one supervised thread remains continuous.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: vellum lift, thread tension, soft wooden table creak

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer B entry
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Open the {{offer_b}} chapter with a distinctive ticket, card, or physical token.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: A teal meetup ticket flips open into the first learning card.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: ticket flick, card hinge, pencil dot

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer B practice
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Show practical workshop, notebook, or hands-on learning objects.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: Workshop cards, a notebook, and a tiny agent token move into a practical table layout.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: index cards sliding, notebook page turn, token tap

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer B progression
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Expand one useful outcome into a coordinated multi-part system.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: One useful-agent card opens into four coordinated cards connected by stitched teal thread.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: four paper folds, thread pulls, soft pin clicks

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer B completion
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Complete a visible learning or adoption path and land on a team outcome.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: A learning path climbs across four raised cards and ends on a circular team badge.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: embossed dots tapping in sequence, paper edge brushes

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer C input
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Fold a messy real-world source into the {{offer_c}} interface.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: A torn recipe-source card folds physically into the paper iPhone.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: thin paper fold, cardstock phone click

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer C transformation
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Return a clean structured result from the interface.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: A clean recipe card slides out of the phone while ingredient sketches pin themselves around it.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: card rail slide, three ingredient taps, pencil scratch

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer C planning
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Arrange the transformed result into a useful plan, grid, or checklist.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: Meal-plan blocks drop into a week grid and check dots descend along a shopping list.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: soft block drops, paper check taps in rhythm

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer C outcome
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Assemble the plan into a satisfying real-world result.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: Paper ingredients assemble into a finished dinner plate and one tissue-paper steam curl rises.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: plate set-down, ingredient rustles, gentle steam hiss

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer D entry
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Introduce {{offer_d}} beside its primary desktop or device surface.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: The black knight cutout lands beside a raised desktop window and wakes the cursor trail.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: wooden token set-down, cardstock window lift, mouse glide

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer D listening
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Show voice, audio, or context being captured and structured.

storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: paper reel turn, pencil chatter, one key click

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer D approval
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Move the action to a visible human approval checkpoint.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: The cursor follows a stitched path to an approval card; the approved side depresses once.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: mouse glide, cardstock button press, shield tap

storyboard_blueprint.title: Offer D companion
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Extend the approved workflow to a companion device without losing continuity.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: A mobile-companion card peels out from the monitor seam and settles beside the desktop.

storyboard_blueprint.title: Ecosystem islands

storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: Learn, build, cook, and work objects land as four distinct paper islands.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: four different tactile object landings

storyboard_blueprint.title: Ecosystem connection
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Connect the offers in narration order with one continuous thread.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: A single stitched thread connects all four islands in narration order.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: continuous thread pull, four pin clicks

storyboard_blueprint.title: Ecosystem motion
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Rotate or orbit the connected system a small physical distance.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: The company wheel rotates one quarter turn while the four islands orbit a small physical distance.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: paper wheel friction, four soft table scrapes

storyboard_blueprint.title: Ecosystem settle
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Land on one clear integrated tableau and let the system settle.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: The connected ecosystem settles into one clear tableau and the thread tension relaxes.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: paper layers settling, quiet room tone

storyboard_blueprint.title: Leader 4 role
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Feature {{leader_4}} with the same scale, treatment, and role-label system.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: Jamie's equally monochrome portrait enters beside classroom notes; EDUCATE is deterministic overlay.

storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Bring all leaders together around the company seal.

storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: four synchronized paper slides, seal thump

storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Snap the four offer cards into one clean two-by-two arrangement.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: The four company chapter cards snap into a clean two-by-two arrangement.

storyboard_blueprint.title: Closing promise
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Reveal {{brand_name}} and {{closing_line}} as deterministic printed overlays.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: A central black torn strip lands; the exact company title and final line appear as deterministic overlays.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: paper strip slap, graphite underline

storyboard_blueprint.title: Final hold
storyboard_blueprint.purpose: Let residual paper motion settle, hold cleanly, then fade to black only at the end.
storyboard_blueprint.motion_reference: Residual paper edges settle for 1.5 seconds, then all motion stops; fade to black only in the final half-second.
storyboard_blueprint.foley_reference: one last paper fiber settle, warm room tone

prompt: Create exactly one current storyboard beat inside a repeatable premium tactile paper-motion brand explainer. Do not attempt the entire long-form program in one generation. Use the supplied plate as the exact starting composition and render only this beat's stated 3–4 second action. Preserve the same physical tabletop set, parchment, torn black cardstock, monochrome pinned photography, kraft paper, restrained accent colors, visible fibers, realistic shadows, object identities, lighting, lens, crop, and layered handcrafted depth across every take. Existing company names, product names, role labels, captions, and logos are fixed printed artwork or deterministic post-production overlays; never redraw, misspell, or invent lettering. Keep motion object-led and physically plausible: one primary paper action, realistic inertia, restrained camera movement, clean native cadence, no synthetic 3D gloss, no random zoom, no scene substitution, no extra objects, no duplicate people, and no visual drift. Follow the beat's camera direction, action, duration, and Foley literally. Complete the main action early enough to leave a clean settling hold. Use LTX for fast production-quality object-led shots and iteration. Upgrade only identity-critical, hero, or difficult high-detail beats to H3, preserving the same plate, timing, and seed family. Return a shot that can cut directly between adjacent beats without changing the shared visual world.

preview.gif_scope: Ten representative one-second samples distributed across the complete 112-second production.

qa_gates: Verify all 32 beats exist, remain in order, match narration timing, and sum to the intended program duration before assembly.
Verify paper stock, palette, scale, lighting, crop, object identities, and physical depth remain continuous across adjacent beats.
Reject invented or misspelled lettering; all names, labels, captions, and logos must come from deterministic overlays or supplied printed plates.
Reject random camera drift, synthetic 3D gloss, duplicate people, extra objects, scene substitution, impossible paper physics, or motion that does not settle cleanly.
Verify the assembled master contains decodable 24 fps H.264 video and AAC audio, full narration, score, Foley, no frozen gaps, and a clean final hold.
Treat the example as a proven internal review candidate, not as Steve-approved final or publication clearance.
